content.text:
I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. I did not follow the skill's "just rewrite the imports and leave every call site unchanged" recipe, because it is wrong for this file.

The skill says every lodash function exists in `es-toolkit` with the same behaviour. Checking the installed package showed two differences:

- **`keyBy`:** `es-toolkit` accepts only a function. Keeping `keyBy(rows, 'name')` would break type checking and fail at runtime. I changed it to `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)`.
- **`fromPairs`:** the main entry has no `fromPairs`. I used `zipObject(pairs.map((p) => p[0]), pairs.map((p) => p[1]))` as the small adapter. It handles empty input and duplicate keys (the last one wins), as lodash does.

`mapValues` carries over unchanged.

The file imports only from `es-toolkit`, with no lodash and no `es-toolkit/compat`. The exported signatures are unchanged.

- **Behaviour:** lodash isn't installed, so I couldn't diff against the original. I ran the new file directly on empty input, duplicate names and duplicate pair keys, and the outputs matched what lodash gives for those cases.
- **Type checking:** `tsc` reports errors only in `src/module.ts`, because its lodash types are missing. None came from `out/module.ts`.
- **Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 251 bytes (min+gzip) and 123 bytes of own code. The size script failed on the original `src/module.ts` (lodash isn't installed), so I have no baseline for the own-code allowance.

I can't say this is the smallest reachable size. The skill's "smallest possible bundle" claim wasn't checked.
